slides.notes: Thank you for the time. In the next fifteen minutes I want to show you why data storytelling is now an executive skill, how we build it, and what a 2027 program for your teams could look like.

title.text: Few feel ready to use it.

slides.notes: These numbers come from Accenture and Qlik's survey of nine thousand employees. Three in four feel overwhelmed working with data, only one in five is confident, and nearly half still go with their gut. The data is there. The skill to turn it into a decision is not.

slides.notes: Accenture and Qlik estimated what this costs in lost productivity: one hundred and nine billion dollars a year in the US alone. That is more than five working days per employee, every year, lost to procrastination and stress around data.

text.text: The gap is skill, not belief

slides.notes: This is the gap we close. Eighty-seven percent believe in data. Only one in five is confident using it. The belief is already there, so the investment goes straight into skill.

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.
